subdivisions.canonical_name: Dale, Gustin and Wallace Addition to Park Ridge
subdivisions.display_name: Dale, Gustin and Wallace Addition to Park Ridge
subdivisions.historical_summary: Dale, Gustin and Wallace Addition is one of the earliest documented Park Ridge additions identified so far. A City of Park Ridge legal memorandum places the plat recording at October 1, 1873 (Document No. 128686 in Cook County), and ties Block 1 lots to addresses in the South Prospect, Courtland, Stewart, and Crescent area.

facts.title: Plat recorded with Cook County
facts.description: Lots 7–17 and 18–23, Block 1, Dale, Gustin and Wallace Addition to Park Ridge, recorded October 1, 1873 as Document No. 128686 in Cook County. Located in part of the Northeast Quarter of Section 35, Township 41 North, Range 12 East of the Third Principal Meridian.

facts.title: Block 1 lots tied to Stewart and Crescent area
facts.description: City memorandum for Special Service Area No. 22-104 identifies lots in Block 1 of Dale, Gustin and Wallace Addition at addresses near South Prospect, Courtland, Stewart, and Crescent.

subdivisions.canonical_name: L. Hodge's Addition to Park Ridge
subdivisions.display_name: L. Hodge's Addition to Park Ridge
subdivisions.historical_summary: L. Hodge's Addition, locally known as 'The Pretzel' for its curving streets, is one of the most historically significant subdivisions in Park Ridge. Multiple City of Park Ridge legal memoranda identify specific lots within the addition, and the city has commissioned an intensive historic survey of the area under an IHPA grant.

facts.title: 36 Main Street identified in Block 5
facts.description: City of Park Ridge memorandum for a special use at 36 Main Street identifies the property as Lot 2, Block 5 in L. Hodge's Addition to Park Ridge, East Half of Section 35, Township 41 North, Range 12 East.

facts.title: 110 South Prospect in Block 1
facts.description: City memorandum for 110 South Prospect Avenue identifies the property as Lots 1 and 2, Block 1 in L. Hodge's Addition to Park Ridge.

facts.title: City approves intensive historic survey
facts.description: The City of Park Ridge approved a historical survey for 'The Pretzel' neighborhood, described as approximately 250 lots in the L. Hodges Addition. The area is locally known for curving streets.

facts.title: City procures technical support for IHPA intensive survey
facts.description: City of Park Ridge engaged technical architectural support for an Intensive Historic Survey of L. Hodges Addition, locally known as 'The Pretzel,' in connection with the city's historic preservation program.
